project.name: mergerag
project.description: A retrieval-augmented generation system that merges retrieved chunks before passing them to the language model, with three strategies (top_k baseline, symmetric concatenation, asymmetric LLM-anchored merging) and pluggable dense or hybrid BM25+dense retrieval.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the top-level mergerag Python package.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the mergerag.core subpackage that exposes shared models, ports, and utilities.

nodes.name: models.py
nodes.summary: Defines the core dataclasses used across the pipeline: Query, Chunk, MergedChunk, MergeOp, MergePlan, Citation, RunTrace, and RunScore.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python dataclasses to declare immutable-ish value objects shared by retriever, merger, and benchmark layers.

nodes.name: Query
nodes.summary: Bundles a query string with its precomputed embedding so retrievers can score it without re-embedding.

nodes.name: Chunk
nodes.summary: Represents a single retrieved passage with id, parent doc id, text, retrieval score, rank, and optional embedding.

nodes.name: MergedChunk
nodes.summary: Output of a merge operation that combines multiple source chunks, tracking provenance via source_chunk_ids and merge_type.

nodes.name: MergeOp
nodes.summary: Describes a single planned merge step with a type tag, primary chunk, and optional secondary chunk.

nodes.name: MergePlan
nodes.summary: Container for an ordered list of MergeOp operations produced by the planner and consumed by the executor.

nodes.name: Citation
nodes.summary: Maps an answer sentence to the chunk ids that support it, parsed out of the LLM response.

nodes.name: RunTrace
nodes.summary: Full trace of a single pipeline run: query, strategy, retrieved/merged chunks, final context, answer, citations, latency, and config snapshot for reproducibility.

nodes.name: RunScore
nodes.summary: Holds Exact Match and F1 scores for a single run/question pair produced by the benchmark scorer.

nodes.name: ports.py
nodes.summary: Declares the hexagonal-architecture port interfaces (EmbedderPort, RetrieverPort, LLMPort, RunStorePort, ScoreStorePort) that adapters must implement.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python Protocol classes to express structural typing for swappable adapters.

nodes.name: EmbedderPort
nodes.summary: Protocol for embedding adapters; defines a single embed(texts) method returning per-text vectors.

nodes.name: RetrieverPort
nodes.summary: Protocol for retrieval adapters with retrieve(query, top_n) and index(documents) methods, implemented by ChromaRetriever and HybridRetriever.

nodes.name: LLMPort
nodes.summary: Protocol for language-model adapters; exposes a complete(prompt, max_tokens) method, currently implemented against Ollama.

nodes.name: RunStorePort
nodes.summary: Protocol for persisting RunTrace objects with save/get/list_runs, backed by SQLite in the default adapter.

nodes.name: ScoreStorePort
nodes.summary: Protocol for persisting RunScore objects (EM/F1) produced by the benchmark scorer.

nodes.name: utils.py
nodes.summary: Small numerical helpers shared across the codebase, currently just a numpy-based cosine similarity used for reranking.

nodes.name: pipeline.py
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the end-to-end MergeRAG flow: embed query, retrieve top_n chunks, optionally plan and execute symmetric/asymmetric merges, rerank by cosine similarity, then prompt the LLM for an answer with citations.
nodes.languageNotes: Stage-level timings logged at DEBUG support the latency profiling work documented in benchmark_findings.md.

nodes.name: _count_tokens
nodes.summary: Approximate token count by summing whitespace-split word counts across chunks.

nodes.name: _parse_citations
nodes.summary: Splits the LLM answer into sentences and extracts bracketed [chunk_id] citations, filtering to ids present in the final context.

nodes.name: _generate_answer
nodes.summary: Loads the answer prompt template, formats it with query and context, calls the LLM, and parses citations from the response.

nodes.name: _within_token_budget
nodes.summary: Greedy selector that keeps chunks in order while their cumulative token count stays under the budget, always keeping at least the first item.

nodes.name: MergeRAGPipeline
nodes.summary: Main pipeline class wired with embedder, retriever, and LLM adapters; the run() method dispatches on strategy (top_k / symmetric / asymmetric) and returns a fully populated RunTrace.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the Streamlit-based frontend app package.

nodes.name: api_client.py
nodes.summary: Thin HTTP client used by the Streamlit UI to POST queries to the MergeRAG API, forwarding all retriever and pipeline knobs and converting non-2xx responses to APIError.

nodes.name: APIError
nodes.summary: Exception raised when the API returns a non-success response or the request fails.

nodes.name: call_query
nodes.summary: Posts a query plus all pipeline parameters (strategy, retriever, top_n/top_k, strong_k, token_budget, asymmetric_max_ops) to the MergeRAG /query endpoint and returns the parsed JSON response.

nodes.name: helpers.py
nodes.summary: Frontend utility helpers for stripping bracketed citations from an answer and computing Exact Match against a gold reference.

nodes.name: streamlit_app.py
nodes.summary: Streamlit UI that runs the three strategies (top_k, symmetric, asymmetric) side-by-side, with sliders for pipeline knobs, a keyword-based smart routing classifier, and per-column rendering of answer, citations, retrieved chunks, and EM score.
nodes.languageNotes: COMPARISON_KEYWORDS list implements the ~87%-accurate keyword classifier referenced in CLAUDE.md.

nodes.name: classify_question
nodes.summary: Lightweight keyword classifier that routes comparison questions to top_k and bridge questions to asymmetric, returning both the type and the chosen strategy.

nodes.name: render_column
nodes.summary: Renders one strategy column in the side-by-side comparison view, showing the answer, EM score, citations, retrieved chunks, and latency metadata.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Top-level project documentation covering the three merge strategies, architecture diagram, project layout, setup, benchmark commands, configuration knobs, and v1-v4 result tables.

nodes.name: corrections.md
nodes.summary: Short running list of code corrections and observations against the project, used as a working notes file.

nodes.name: pyproject.toml
nodes.summary: Python project metadata and dependency declaration covering runtime, optional, and dev dependency groups plus pytest configuration.

nodes.name: benchmark_findings.md
nodes.summary: Detailed write-up of four HotpotQA benchmark runs (v1 baseline, v2 fixes, v3 hybrid retriever, v4 qwen2.5:7b), per-question-type breakdowns, profile results, and key findings on merge strategy efficacy.

nodes.name: answer.txt
nodes.summary: Prompt template loaded by the pipeline to instruct the LLM to answer using the provided context and cite chunk ids in brackets.

nodes.name: merge_asymmetric.txt
nodes.summary: Prompt template used by the asymmetric merge executor to anchor a weak chunk to a strong one via the LLM.

nodes.name: merge_symmetric.txt
nodes.summary: Prompt template historically used for symmetric merge synthesis; the current sym_fixed implementation skips this LLM call in favor of plain concatenation.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the adapters subpackage that hosts concrete implementations of core ports (embedder, LLM, retriever, stores).

nodes.name: embedder.py
nodes.summary: SentenceTransformer-based embedder adapter implementing EmbedderPort, defaulting to the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model.

nodes.name: SentenceTransformerEmbedder
nodes.summary: Wraps a SentenceTransformer model and exposes an embed() method that returns Python lists for downstream consumers.

nodes.name: llm.py
nodes.summary: Ollama-backed LLM adapter implementing LLMPort, defaulting to the qwen2.5:3b model with a configurable max_tokens budget.

nodes.name: OllamaLLM
nodes.summary: Thin client around the ollama Python SDK that issues a single generate call and returns the response text.

nodes.name: retriever.py
nodes.summary: Retriever adapters layering dense Chroma vector search, BM25 sparse retrieval, and a hybrid retriever that fuses both via Reciprocal Rank Fusion.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses chromadb for dense ANN search and rank_bm25 for sparse retrieval; RRF k=60 follows the original Cormack et al. recipe.

nodes.name: ChromaRetriever
nodes.summary: Dense vector retriever that wraps a Chroma collection with cosine similarity, supporting indexing, full-corpus dumps, and embedding-based retrieval.

nodes.name: BM25Index
nodes.summary: In-memory BM25Okapi index over a chunk list, tokenizing on lowercased alphanumeric runs for sparse keyword retrieval.

nodes.name: HybridRetriever
nodes.summary: Composite retriever that combines a ChromaRetriever and a BM25Index, refreshing the sparse arm when the collection changes and fusing results with RRF.

nodes.name: rrf_fuse
nodes.summary: Reciprocal Rank Fusion of dense and sparse result lists with smoothing constant k=60, returning chunks ranked by summed reciprocal-rank scores.

nodes.name: run_store.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed persistence for RunTrace objects, serializing retrieved chunks, merged chunks, final context, merge plans, and citations to JSON columns.

nodes.name: SQLiteRunStore
nodes.summary: Implements RunStorePort against SQLite with INSERT OR REPLACE save semantics and pagination over runs ordered by creation time.

nodes.name: score_store.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed persistence for per-run RunScore records capturing exact-match and F1 evaluation outputs alongside the gold answer.

nodes.name: SQLiteScoreStore
nodes.summary: Implements ScoreStorePort with a flat scores table keyed by run_id, supporting upsert save and time-ordered listing.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Public surface of the ingestion subpackage, re-exporting load_document, ParagraphChunker, and ingest_document.

nodes.name: chunker.py
nodes.summary: Paragraph-based text chunker that greedily merges paragraphs up to max_chars and folds short trailing pieces into the previous chunk for deterministic Chunk IDs.

nodes.name: ParagraphChunker
nodes.summary: Splits documents on double newlines, greedily merges paragraphs under a max_chars budget, and emits Chunk objects with deterministic zero-padded IDs.

nodes.name: ingest.py
nodes.summary: Top-level ingestion orchestrator that loads a document, chunks it, embeds the chunks, and indexes them via the injected retriever.

nodes.name: ingest_document
nodes.summary: Loads a file, chunks it with an optional ParagraphChunker, embeds the chunks, and writes them into the retriever, returning the chunk count.

nodes.name: loader.py
nodes.summary: Loads .txt and .md documents from disk, stripping fenced code blocks and HTML tags from Markdown before returning the raw text.

nodes.name: load_document
nodes.summary: Reads a text or Markdown file and returns a (doc_id, normalized text) tuple, raising on unsupported extensions.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the merge subpackage, which contains the planner, executor, and per-strategy modules.

nodes.name: executor.py
nodes.summary: Executes a MergePlan by concatenating symmetric pairs (no LLM call) and using LLM synthesis only for asymmetric merges, mitigating small-model hallucination.
nodes.languageNotes: Symmetric concatenation was introduced after the n=500 run showed qwen2.5:3b hallucinating on weak-pair synthesis.

nodes.name: execute
nodes.summary: Iterates merge operations and produces MergedChunk objects, branching between text concatenation for symmetric and LLM-prompted synthesis for other types.

nodes.name: planner.py
nodes.summary: Pure planning function that partitions retrieved chunks into strong and weak sets and dispatches to symmetric or asymmetric strategies to build a MergePlan.

nodes.name: plan
nodes.summary: Splits chunks at strong_k and routes the weak tail to pair_weak_chunks or assign_to_anchors based on strategy, capping asymmetric ops.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker grouping the symmetric and asymmetric merge strategy modules.

nodes.name: asymmetric.py
nodes.summary: Asymmetric merge strategy that anchors each weak chunk to its nearest same-doc strong chunk, sorts candidates by similarity, and caps merges to bound latency.

nodes.name: assign_to_anchors
nodes.summary: Pairs each weak chunk with its best same-doc strong anchor above min_similarity, then returns up to max_ops asymmetric MergeOps ordered by similarity.

nodes.name: symmetric.py
nodes.summary: Symmetric merge strategy that greedily pairs weak chunks by highest mutual cosine similarity within the same document, skipping low-similarity pairs.

nodes.name: pair_weak_chunks
nodes.summary: Greedy O(n^2) pairing of weak chunks that selects each chunk's best remaining partner above min_similarity, restricted to same-document pairs by default.

nodes.name: __init__.py
nodes.summary: Empty package marker for the evaluation subpackage that hosts the benchmark orchestrator and scoring helpers.

nodes.name: benchmark.py
nodes.summary: Benchmark orchestrator that ingests a HotpotQA fixture, runs the pipeline across configured strategies, scores answers with EM/F1, persists traces, and aggregates per-strategy summaries.

nodes.name: _ingest_corpus
nodes.summary: Materializes every unique HotpotQA context document to a temp file and feeds it through ingest_document so the retriever's index reflects the fixture.

nodes.name: _compute_summary
nodes.summary: Aggregates per-strategy mean EM, F1, latency, and token counts from the run results into a StrategyStats summary map.

nodes.name: _filter_active_asymmetric_examples
nodes.summary: Pre-runs the planner in asymmetric mode against each question and keeps only those where at least one merge op would fire, enabling targeted asymmetric benchmarking.

nodes.name: run_benchmark
nodes.summary: Top-level benchmark loop that ingests the corpus, builds the pipeline, iterates examples and strategies, scores each run, persists traces and scores, and assembles a BenchmarkResult.

nodes.name: _answer_for_scoring
nodes.summary: Cleans citation tags from a pipeline answer and falls back to extracting bracketed chunk-id stems so malformed outputs still score sensibly.

nodes.name: scorer.py
nodes.summary: Implements SQuAD-style normalization, exact-match, and token-overlap F1 scoring used for evaluating HotpotQA answers.

nodes.name: f1
nodes.summary: Computes token-overlap F1 between a predicted and gold answer after SQuAD-style normalization, handling empty-string edge cases.

nodes.name: benchmark_cli.py
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point that wires up embedder, retriever (chroma or hybrid), LLM, and SQLite stores, then runs the benchmark and writes a JSON results report.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses CLI arguments, optionally resets the Chroma collection, builds all adapters, runs the benchmark, prints a summary table, and serializes per-run results to JSON.

nodes.name: ingest_cli.py
nodes.summary: Command-line entry point that ingests a single .txt or .md file into a Chroma collection using the SentenceTransformer embedder.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses --path, --collection, and --persist-path, constructs embedder and retriever, calls ingest_document, and reports the indexed chunk count.

nodes.summary: Profiling script that attaches a logging handler to capture per-stage latencies across strategies and prints aggregate statistics including asymmetric merge fire rates.

nodes.summary: Custom logging handler that parses pipeline stage-latency log lines into structured rows for downstream aggregation.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand MergeRAG's core idea: individual retrieved chunks are often weak in isolation, so the system pairs or anchors them before generation to tighten the LLM's context window. The README lays out the three merge strategies (top_k, symmetric, asymmetric), the two retrievers (dense Chroma, hybrid BM25+dense), the hexagonal architecture, and the v1–v4 benchmark results. Read this first to align the rest of the tour against the project's intended narrative.

tour.title: Core Domain Model
tour.description: The whole pipeline communicates through a small set of dataclasses defined here: Query (text + embedding), Chunk and MergedChunk (the units retrieval and merging produce), MergeOp and MergePlan (a merge recipe), Citation, and RunTrace/RunScore for persistence. With 25 inbound dependencies, this file is the single most depended-on module in the codebase — every adapter, route, and test ultimately speaks this vocabulary.
tour.languageLesson: Python dataclasses (@dataclass) give you typed records with auto-generated __init__, __repr__, and __eq__. Combined with type hints and Optional, they replace dict-shaped payloads with self-documenting structures that IDEs and type-checkers can validate.

tour.title: Hexagonal Ports
tour.description: ports.py declares the five protocol interfaces — EmbedderPort, RetrieverPort, LLMPort, RunStorePort, ScoreStorePort — that the rest of the system depends on. This is the seam that makes MergeRAG pluggable: the pipeline never imports a concrete embedder or LLM, it only asks for something that satisfies the port. Step 4 will show how the adapters fulfil these contracts.
tour.languageLesson: Python's typing.Protocol enables structural (duck) typing for static checks: any class with the right method signatures satisfies the protocol without needing to inherit from it. This is how hexagonal architecture stays idiomatic in Python instead of requiring abstract base classes.

tour.title: Adapters: Embedder, LLM, Stores
tour.description: These concrete adapters plug into the ports from Step 3. The embedder wraps SentenceTransformer (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 by default), the LLM adapter talks to a local Ollama daemon (qwen2.5:3b default), and the two SQLite-backed stores persist RunTrace and RunScore records. Each one is small and single-purpose because the port already specifies the contract.

tour.title: Retrieval: Dense, BM25, and Hybrid
tour.description: retriever.py contains three layered adapters: ChromaRetriever for dense cosine search, BM25Index for sparse keyword scoring, and HybridRetriever which fuses both via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF k=60). The hybrid path is what the README's v3 numbers measure — BM25 fixes entity recall while dense covers semantic matches. The user picks one at request time through PipelineParams.
tour.languageLesson: Reciprocal Rank Fusion combines ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) across each source. It's hyperparameter-light (one constant k) and ignores raw scores, which lets you fuse heterogeneous retrievers (BM25 vs cosine) without calibration.

tour.title: Ingestion: Load, Chunk, Index
tour.description: Before retrieval can happen, documents must be loaded from disk, split into paragraph-sized chunks, embedded, and pushed into Chroma. loader.py strips fenced code blocks and HTML from .txt/.md inputs, chunker.py greedily merges paragraphs up to max_chars and folds short trailing pieces back, and ingest.py composes the embedder and retriever to index the result. This is the offline half of the system — query time only reads from what ingestion writes.

tour.title: The MergeRAG Pipeline
tour.description: pipeline.py is the heart of the system: embed query → retrieve top_n → split strong/weak by score threshold → plan merges → execute merges → re-embed merged chunks → rerank by cosine → truncate to context budget → prompt the LLM. The same orchestrator handles all three strategies; the strategy argument only changes how the planner decides what to merge. The answer.txt prompt template tells the LLM to cite chunk IDs in brackets, which the API then parses into Citation objects.

tour.title: Merge Strategies: Planner and Executor
tour.description: The merge logic is split in two for testability. planner.py is a pure function that partitions chunks into strong vs weak by score and dispatches to a strategy module to build a MergePlan. executor.py then runs the plan: symmetric pairs are concatenated with no LLM call (the Q1 fix from the README that eliminated qwen2.5:3b hallucination), while asymmetric pairs invoke the LLM with merge_asymmetric.txt to anchor a weak chunk against a strong one. asymmetric.py caps merges via max_ops to bound latency (the Q3 fix).

tour.title: FastAPI HTTP Layer
tour.description: app.py is the FastAPI application factory: it builds the embedder, LLM, run store, and Chroma client once per process via a lifespan handler and mounts the four routers. deps.py provides per-request dependencies and caches HybridRetriever instances per collection (BM25 indices are expensive to build). config.py exposes tunable defaults through pydantic-settings so deployments can override models, paths, and top_n via environment variables.

tour.title: HTTP Endpoints and Schemas
tour.description: The four routers expose the system over HTTP: POST /query runs the pipeline with caller-supplied PipelineParams and persists the trace, POST /ingest streams an upload through the ingestion pipeline, /collections lists and deletes Chroma collections (invalidating the hybrid cache), and /runs paginates the saved RunTraces. schemas.py defines the pydantic request/response DTOs (including a discriminated union for raw vs merged context items) and serializers.py maps core dataclasses to those DTOs.
tour.languageLesson: FastAPI's APIRouter lets you group endpoints by feature and mount them onto an app at startup. Combined with Depends() injection, routes stay declarative — they ask for a pipeline or settings object and FastAPI resolves it from the dependency graph.

tour.title: Streamlit Frontend
tour.description: streamlit_app.py is the user-facing surface: it renders the three strategies side-by-side, exposes sliders for every pipeline knob (top_n, top_k, retriever, asymmetric_max_ops, etc.), routes queries through a keyword-based smart classifier, and shows answer, citations, retrieved chunks, and EM score per column. It never touches the pipeline directly — api_client.py POSTs to the FastAPI server from Step 9, and helpers.py strips citation brackets and computes EM against the gold reference.

tour.title: Evaluation and Benchmarking
tour.description: The evaluation layer is how every claim in the README was measured. benchmark.py iterates a HotpotQA fixture, runs each configured strategy through the pipeline, scores answers with SQuAD-style EM and token-overlap F1, and persists per-strategy aggregates. benchmark_cli.py is the entry point used to produce the v1–v4 result files in results/, and profile_latency.py attaches a logging handler to measure stage timings (the Q3 work that surfaced asymmetric's 26s merge stage).
